newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran's Bandar Abbas gas oil exports possible Q1 98.
newsitem.headline: Iran's Bandar Abbas gas oil exports possible Q1 98.

text.p: Gas oil exports from Iran's new Bandar Abbas refinery could begin in the first quarter of next year, Deputy Oil Minister Hojatollah Ghanimifard said on Thursday.
But exports would depend on winter fuel demand in Iran and a continuation of existing middle distillate and gasoline supply contracts from Iran's northern neighbours.
"If everything goes normal we think this a thing (export gas oil) we can do," Ghanimifard said.
Azerbaijan and Turmenistan supply products to Iran, though Ghanimifard said these imports could be affected if demand increased in the Central Asian states during the winter.

Operations at the export-orientated 232,000 barrels per day (bpd) Bandar Abbas plant at the mouth of the Gulf began in June, though exports have so far been limited to straight-run fuel oil based on one operational crude distillation unit.
Full operations are not expected to be reached till late 1998.
